subject.title: Gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages

question: Which restart message-loss path should own this issue: the SQLite-backed followup recovery PR, the SIGUSR1 drain mitigation, or a successor design?
rationale: Current main still has the bug, but there are multiple open partial/candidate PRs and repository policy makes the storage and replay semantics a product/architecture choice rather than a narrow repair job.

options.title: Advance SQLite recovery
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a successor as the canonical durable followup-queue recovery path, after it satisfies context, upgrade, and exact-once proof requirements.

options.title: Keep SIGUSR1 drain separate
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/46303 as a partial mitigation for debounce/drain timing and do not let it replace durable replay.

options.title: Pause for successor design
options.body: Close or pause the current candidate PRs only if maintainers want a fresh design that combines queue persistence, drain-window capture, and provider ACK policy.

recommendation.title: Advance SQLite recovery
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82572 or a successor as the canonical durable followup-queue recovery path, after it satisfies context, upgrade, and exact-once proof requirements.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged restart-drain work and queue singleton history make this the best available routing candidate for the restart lifecycle decision.
